output.summary: Evidence does not show an attrition crisis: trailing-12-month associate attrition is 14.1% against a 15.0% firm average and an 18.0% peer median. Seniors are at 13.6%, against a 5-year average of 14.0% and a peer median of 17.5%. Clustered resignations have happened before. Both September leavers had independent reasons (a client GC role and a spouse's residency) and said the Friday change was not a factor. Complaints are real but concentrated on the deliberate, accepted end of remote Fridays. Flexibility satisfaction fell, but intent to stay did not. The training rise is confounded with the new curriculum and the first-year cohort. A bonus or an early reversal is premature. Keep the policy under its monitoring triggers, explain its rationale to associates, and consider edge accommodations.
